title: Depth 14 (dim 896, 14 heads of 64)
description: DEPTH 10->14 (n_embd 640->896 via ASPECT_RATIO 64), HEAD_DIM 128->64 (14 heads of 64), DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->32 (grad_accum 4) for VRAM headroom; all LRs and schedules untouched.
reflection: Strong NEGATIVE: val_bpb 1.033314 vs 0.988076 baseline, +0.0452 (~64 sigma against the 7e-4 noise floor). 478 steps, 125.3M tokens, 200.9M params, MFU 43.39%, peak VRAM 34.4GB. This includes HEAD_DIM 64, which a2 measured at -0.0038, so depth 14 on its own cost roughly +0.049. The depth axis has turned over hard between 10 and 14. Throughput is NOT the cause: MFU actually rose monotonically with size (38.7% at depth 8, 41.9% at depth 10, 43.4% here), so the GPU is being used better than ever - the model is simply starved of data, seeing only 125M tokens for 201M params. VRAM is also not the constraint (34GB of 80GB). Fitting a quadratic through the three head64-consistent points in log-params (d8 ~0.9935 at 50M, d10 ~0.984 adjusted at 86M, d14 1.0333 at 201M) puts the minimum at ~77M params, i.e. depth ~9.6 - essentially the current baseline - and predicts depth 12 at ~1.000, worse than depth 10. Secondary finding worth carrying: value_embeds are 51.4M of the 201M params here (7 tables of 8192x896), growing as depth*dim, so scaling depth inflates a component that gets AdamW at embedding_lr rather than adding transformer capacity.
